Chapter 9

Newton-Cartan Theory

Motivation: Gravity as geometry: Newton’s theory on spacetime

In Newtonian mechanics, a particle of mass \(m\), described in Cartesian coordinates of an inertial frame, obeys \[ m \, \ddot{\gamma}^\alpha_\mathcal{U}(t) = f^\alpha_\gamma(t) - m \, \partial_\alpha \Phi\big( t, \gamma_\mathcal{U}(t) \big), \qquad \sum_\alpha \partial_\alpha \partial_\alpha \Phi = 4 \pi G_N \, \rho , \] where \(f^\alpha_\gamma\) are the components of the forces acting on it and \(\Phi\) is the gravitational potential, determined by the mass density \(\rho\). The gravitational term is unlike any other force: it is proportional to the very mass that measures inertia, so \(m\) drops out of free fall, \(\ddot{\gamma}^\alpha_\mathcal{U} = - \partial_\alpha \Phi\), and all bodies fall alike. The pseudo-forces of rotating or accelerated frames, such as the Coriolis and centrifugal forces, share this property, and they are not caused by any body: they are produced by the choice of frame. This suggests treating gravity not as a force, but as part of the geometry, as what “straight” means. On space this fails (Appendix B.21.4), but on spacetime, the speed is part of the direction of the worldline, and the idea works.

Goal: reformulate Newtonian gravity on a 4-dimensional manifold, with gravity encoded in a connection.

  • Define a Newtonian spacetime: an absolute time \(t\) and a torsion-free connection \(\nabla\) along which time flows uniformly, with no notion of spatial distance.

  • Rephrase Newton’s axioms: free particles follow the autoparallels of \(\nabla\), forces are measured as deviations from them, and absolute time is singled out as the parameter of every worldline.

  • In charts adapted to absolute time, identify the pseudo-forces (Coriolis, centrifugal, Euler, translational) with connection coefficient functions created by the chart alone.

  • Place gravity in the connection: uniform gravity is a pseudo-force, removed in a freely falling chart, whereas non-uniform gravity is curvature, which no chart removes. Poisson’s equation becomes a condition on the Ricci curvature, and the Riemann curvature measures the tidal acceleration.

Already in Newton’s theory, gravity is the curvature of spacetime. General relativity (Chapter 10) keeps this insight and replaces absolute time by a Lorentzian metric and time orientation.
